check_text:
01-one-shot.py: 1 biology problem (1 warning).

1. WARNING UNMIXED-AT-END: 12 wells never mixed after plasmid 1, plasmid 2, plasmid 3,
plasmid 4 and 8 more went in (25% of the well)
   line 97:  p20.dispense(5, dest_well)
   At line 97 the robot added plasmid 1, plasmid 2, plasmid 3, plasmid 4 and 8 more to wells
   A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8 and 4 more in slot 3, which already held water, buffer and
   enzyme (this line did it 12 times). The addition was 25% of the well, nothing mixed the
   well afterwards, and the run ended with them that way. Two liquids layered in a small
   well do not mix on their own, so what the well holds is not at the concentration you
   calculated. The liquid added last is a sample, so nothing else in the workflow will mix
   it: a normalisation or a pool left like this is not what it says it is.
   Affected: wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8 and 4 more in slot 3.
   Fix: Mix wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8 and 4 more in slot 3 after line 97:
   `mix_after=(5, 16)` on the transfer, or `pipette.mix(5, 16, well)`, with the volume about
   80% of what the well holds.
   Source: Artel: automated liquid handlers as sources of error
           https://www.bioprocessintl.com/assays/automated-liquid-handlers-as-sources-of-error
   Source: Illumina: normalising library concentrations (pipette up and down 10 times to
   mix)
           https://support.illumina.com/ko-kr/bulletins/2017/03/best-practices-for-manually-normalizing-library-concentrations.html
   Source: Thermo PowerTrack user guide (a reaction plate not mixed well gives variable
   replicates)
           https://documents.thermofisher.com/TFS-Assets/LSG/manuals/MAN0018825_PowerTrackSYBRGreenMasterMix_UG.pdf
   Source: Integra: how to perform serial dilutions
           https://www.integra-biosciences.com/global/en/applicationguide/master-art-pipetting-and-learn-how-perform-serial-dilutions-our-comprehensive-guide
   [79753bb8b3de]

The Opentrons simulator (8.8.2) passed this protocol with no error: it checks that the robot
can make the moves, not what they do to the liquids.
